input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Compliant at (in fact above) the preferred position; resubmitted unchanged in substance because the verifier feedback affirms every element of the analysis and identifies no unaddressed defect. Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side obligation to "indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer" and its personnel against all third-party Claims, including reasonable attorneys' fees. Its limbs are subject-matter triggers rather than cause-of-action triggers: "(i) the Services;" "(ii) the Auction Platform;" (iii) Creative placed onto Customer's platforms or websites by the Auction Platform; "(iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder." A third-party allegation that the Services, Auction Platform or delivered Creative infringe or misappropriate IP is a Claim "arising out of or in connection with" limbs (i)-(iii), and Vendor misconduct falls within (iv)-(v). The deterministic check for "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" fails only as a phrasing artefact: the clause never uses the words "infringe" or "intellectual property", but the substantive scope the rule requires is present. I have not reclassified to deviation to make that check pass, because the playbook's classification semantics turn on material terms rather than wording, and redlining a clause that already exceeds the fallback and benefits us would be wrong. The clause also beats the fallback: no Customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs, no procure/modify/replace/refund sole-remedy limitation, no 3x super-cap, and Section 7(a) expressly excludes indemnification liability from the consequential-damages waiver. Section 11 supplies the preferred procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnitor control of defence and settlement, no liability-admitting settlement without the indemnified party's consent, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost). Two sub-preferred points are noted for leverage only, not redlined: the reciprocal Customer indemnity in Section 10(b) is broader than "Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law" (it also reaches unauthorised use, breach of warranty and Customer acts/omissions), and the Creative limb is qualified by "to the best of its knowledge". Residual risk for the negotiating team: the IP conclusion rests on reading "in connection with the Services", which a vendor could later argue reaches only performance-related claims; an express IP-infringement limb is a low-cost clarifying ask that would not weaken anything we already have.
